statusText: CME equity futures are halted for eleven of the twenty-four published hours and no U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside the window, holding Tail at the closed-venue floor. Every Friday primary mark re-verified unchanged this run. The ledger gained detail on both sides: the 16 September hike to 3.75-4.00% with a dot plot pointing to one more increase, against a Saudi pipeline restart that has eased the physical oil panic for a third consecutive session.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 5 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. The 22:00Z restart is published at Tail 18, the window high and still inside the EA_ON band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: A hiking Fed and 100-dollar crude sit against an easing Hormuz supply panic and a two-session equity rebound: every primary mark re-verifies unchanged and a genuinely two-sided weekend still points to two-way discovery at the 22:00Z restart
body:
Eleven of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the remaining thirteen contain the 22:00Z restart, the hours after it and the Asian and early European sessions that follow. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September and there has been no live NQ price path since 21:00Z that day. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run and every one is unchanged: the Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a previous close of 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08% from 15.44, inside a 14.80-15.63 day range and near the lower end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range. WTI settled 100.30 and Brent 103.87, a third consecutive easier session, although WTI remains up about 18.85% over the month. Federal Reserve H.15 shows the 2-year at 4.67% and the 10-year at 4.94%.

Two items sharpened the ledger this run without changing its balance. On the restrictive side, the 16 September FOMC raised the target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00%, the first increase since 2023, with a dot plot pointing to one more move this year and a raised inflation forecast; that is the backdrop against which the 10-year sits near 4.94% and equity valuations have to work. On the permissive side, Saudi Aramco is reported to be partially restarting its East-West pipeline within days, ship-to-ship transfers near Sohar have restored Hormuz routing, and the physical supply panic is described as easing, which is why crude fell for a third session even as an IRGC strike on a Togo-flagged tanker on 17 September and warnings against unapproved transits remain outstanding. Crude net-long positioning is reported at its heaviest since late May, a crowded-book risk that belongs to Stress rather than Tail.

That balance is why the published scores separate the way they do. Stress holds at 31 in the moderate band, carrying oil-led inflation risk, a hiking Fed, elevated long-end yields and a catalyst-dense week. Tail holds at 5 because Tail measures a pathological price path that denies retracement, and a halted venue cannot exhibit one; equally, a VIX of 14.81 and a Friday close near the day's high are not evidence of that path either. Dominant mode is normal because no venue is open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence of 76 reflects fully re-verified levels, yields, crude, volatility and a verified seven-day calendar; the single gap, live price-path evidence, is structural to the weekend halt rather than a defect in the research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 through the first eleven slots, eased to 4 from 22:00Z Saturday through 04:00Z Sunday and returned to 5 across the final six slots. Stress opened at 22, drifted through 23 and 24 across Saturday afternoon and evening, stepped to 26 after midnight, eased to 25, then jumped to 29 at 05:00Z as the weekend escalation reporting landed and climbed to 30 and finally 31. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence began at 75, troughed at 72 at 21:00Z Saturday as distance from the Friday tape grew, and recovered into the mid-70s as weekend reporting was corroborated.
outlookSummary: Eleven of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the remaining thirteen contain the 22:00Z restart and the Asian and European hours after it. Cash closed Friday 18 September and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday, 18:00 ET. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window; the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday in the final published hour, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 5 for the current hour and the next, then steps through 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 across the European Sunday afternoon and evening before reaching 13 and 15 in the two pre-restart hours. It tops the window at 18 at the 22:00Z restart, eases to 17 for the first full hour, then decays through 15, 14, 13, 12, 11 and 10 across the Asian session before ticking to 11 at the European cash open and again at 10:00Z for the Goolsbee checkpoint. That drift tracks time-to-restart and session transitions rather than observed structure, and every published hour stays inside the EA_ON band. Stress holds between 30 and 35, peaking at the restart. Confidence troughs at 71 immediately before and at the restart, then rises to 78 as a live tape re-accumulates.
